headline: Every cell in your body was built from food you ate—you literally are what you eat
universal_truth: Inputs become outputs; what you take in shapes what you become
fun_facts: Your body replaces most cells every 7-10 years—the material comes from food
The atoms in your body right now were once in other living things—and will be again
Digestion breaks food down to molecular building blocks, which your body reassembles into you
discussion_questions: How does knowing food becomes you change how you think about eating?
What else do you 'consume' that becomes part of you?
How does the quality of inputs affect the quality of outputs?

hook.script: The cells in your body are built from food you ate. That apple, that sandwich, that salad—their molecules were disassembled and reassembled into you. You are literally constructed from what you consume. 'You are what you eat' isn't metaphor—it's biology.

cliff.script: Food seems to disappear when we eat it. But where does it actually go? How does a meal become muscle, bone, and brain?

options.text: Digestion breaks food into molecular components that are absorbed and rebuilt into body structures
options.response: Yes. Your digestive system is a disassembly line; your cells are the rebuild crew. Proteins become your proteins. Fats become your fats. You're constantly rebuilding yourself from raw materials.

options.text: Food provides energy that powers body processes
options.response: Energy is one use, but food also provides the physical building materials that become your body...

fact1.title: Molecular Lego
fact1.script: Digestion breaks food into basic molecules: amino acids, fatty acids, sugars. These are absorbed into your blood and distributed to cells. Your cells then reassemble these blocks into new proteins, membranes, and structures. Same blocks, new you.

fact2.title: Constant Renewal
fact2.script: Your body replaces most of its cells over 7-10 years. Skin cells last weeks, red blood cells months, bone cells years. The material for every replacement comes from food. You're constantly rebuilding yourself from what you eat.

fact3.title: Atoms Cycle
fact3.script: The atoms in your body were once in other living things—plants, animals, ancient organisms. After you, they'll become part of something else. You're a temporary arrangement of atoms borrowed from the world and recycled through food.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Inputs become outputs. What you take in shapes what you become—literally, with food. This applies beyond nutrition: what you read, watch, and think also shapes who you are. Choose your inputs wisely.

outro.script: That's Day 130. Tomorrow, we continue exploring cultures and human achievement. Until then, at your next meal, consider that those molecules will become part of you.

growTrack.title: Input Awareness - Choose What Becomes You
growTrack.learning_objective: Connect inputs to their effects on who you become
growTrack.activity: At your next meal, consider: these molecules will be disassembled and rebuilt into my body. Does that change what you want to eat? Then expand the thought: what other 'inputs'—information, media, relationships—are shaping who you become?
